entities.name: Edward Neville, 3rd Baron Bergavenny
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Edward Neville (c. 1414 – October 27, 1476) was an English nobleman whose strategic marital alliance and unwavering loyalty to the House of York during the tumultuous Wars of the Roses cemented the Neville family's claim to the ancient Barony of Bergavenny. As the de facto 3rd Baron Bergavenny, his life intersected with a period of profound dynastic conflict that reshaped the English aristocracy and monarchy. Born the sixth son of Ralph Neville, 1st Earl of Westmorland, and Joan Beaufort, daughter of John of Gaunt, Edward was deeply embedded within England's most powerful noble network, making him a critical, if sometimes overlooked, participant in the 15th-century power struggles.

Neville's ascent to the peerage was largely through his marriage to Elizabeth Beauchamp, the de jure 3rd Baroness Bergavenny, whose ancestral title he held *jure uxoris* (by right of his wife). Following Elizabeth's death in 1448, Edward was controversially summoned to Parliament in 1450 as Baron Bergavenny in his own right, a move that solidified the Neville name with this ancient barony, circumventing a potential lapse of the title. During the Wars of the Roses, he was a staunch Yorkist, fighting for Edward IV at pivotal engagements such as the Battle of Towton in 1461, a decisive victory for the Yorkist cause. His loyalty was rewarded with various offices, including Constable of Dover Castle and Lord Warden of the Cinque Ports, further entrenching his family's influence in the south-east of England.
